alt.en: A printed book page headed "Prose on the Nativity. xiii" and "Another Prose on the Nativity of our Lord. Sixth Tone. G. major." Eight staves of square-note plainchant, joined in pairs, carry the Latin "Adeste fideles laeti triumphantes, venite, venite in Bethlehem" and "Venite adoremus Dominum", with two more Latin lines printed below.
alt.es: Página impresa de un libro con los encabezados "Prose on the Nativity. xiii" y "Another Prose on the Nativity of our Lord. Sixth Tone. G. major." Ocho pentagramas de canto llano con notas cuadradas, unidos de dos en dos, llevan el latín "Adeste fideles laeti triumphantes, venite, venite in Bethlehem" y "Venite adoremus Dominum", con otras dos líneas en latín impresas debajo.

caption.en: Adeste fideles as "Another Prose on the Nativity of our Lord" in An Essay on the Church Plain Chant (London, 1782), the earliest known printing of the tune in the even four-beat time sung today.
caption.es: Adeste fideles como "Another Prose on the Nativity of our Lord" en An Essay on the Church Plain Chant (Londres, 1782), la primera impresión conocida de la melodía en el compás regular de cuatro tiempos que se canta hoy.

source: An Essay on the Church Plain Chant, part second, containing several anthems, litanies, ... as they are sung in the public chapels at London (London, 1782), p. xiii
library: Internet Archive, Eighteenth Century collection (from microfilm)
licenceEvidence: Printed London 1782; anonymous, or by Samuel Webbe (died 1816) if he prepared it; Wade died 1786. Faithful microfilm scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).

alt.en: A printed hymnal page headed "Nativity" with hymn 89, "Adeste Fideles. P. M. Irregular", marked "Anon. 1751 (?)". Four-part music on paired staves in A major and 4/4 carries three verses beginning "Oh come, all ye faithful", "Sing, choirs of Angels" and "Yea, Lord, we greet Thee", and the refrain "Oh come, let us adore Him" marked "After each verse". At the foot: "Anon. (Latin, 17th Cent.) Tr. F. Oakeley, 1841" and page number 63.
alt.es: Página impresa de un himnario con el encabezado "Nativity" y el himno 89, "Adeste Fideles. P. M. Irregular", marcado "Anon. 1751 (?)". La música a cuatro voces, en pentagramas emparejados, en La mayor y 4/4, lleva tres estrofas que empiezan "Oh come, all ye faithful", "Sing, choirs of Angels" y "Yea, Lord, we greet Thee", y el estribillo "Oh come, let us adore Him", marcado "After each verse". Al pie: "Anon. (Latin, 17th Cent.) Tr. F. Oakeley, 1841" y el número de página 63.

caption.en: No. 89 in Hymns of Worship and Service (New York, 1909): Oakeley's English as Murray's hymnal of 1852 changed it, with the refrain after each verse, the page our arrangement is read from.
caption.es: El n.º 89 de Hymns of Worship and Service (Nueva York, 1909): la versión inglesa de Oakeley con los cambios del himnario de Murray de 1852 y el estribillo después de cada estrofa, la página de la que sale nuestro arreglo.

source: Hymns of Worship and Service (New York: The Century Co., 1909), No. 89, "Adeste Fideles", p. 63
